events.reason: Sudden change in vision, right eye

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY PHYSICIAN DOCUMENTATION -- outside hospital
Arrival 02/12/2025 07:05

CC: R eye vision changed this AM

HPI: 27M with Marfan syndrome and known bilateral lens subluxation, evaluated by cardiology about a year ago for aortic regurgitation. Woke up, rubbed his right eye lightly, and his vision in that eye abruptly shifted -- blurry and "off." No injury beyond the rub. No eye pain. No headache.

PMH: Marfan syndrome (FBN1); aortic root aneurysm 4.2 cm; chronic severe AR; MVP with mild MR, diagnosed last year; bilateral ectopia lentis. Tall with long extremities.
PSH: dental extraction 2024 (antibiotic prophylaxis).
Meds: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: father Marfan, prophylactic root replacement at 38; paternal uncle sudden death at 31, presumed dissection; mother healthy; younger sister with Marfan.
SHx: never smoker; EtOH 1-2/month; graduate student, library sciences.

Exam:
VS: BP 130/70, HR 78, afebrile.
General: 6'4", arm span exceeds height, comfortable.
Eyes: right lens displaced up and toward the nose. Conjunctiva white, no injection. Fluorescein: no corneal abrasion. No redness.
CV: midsystolic click, then a late systolic murmur at the apex.
Remainder of exam unremarkable.

MDM: painless acute visual change from progression of known right lens subluxation after minor rubbing. No signs of trauma, globe injury or angle closure. Habitus marfanoid, consistent with his known diagnosis.

Impression: right ectopia lentis, acute progression of subluxation.
Disposition: home. Eye shield not required. Ophthalmology referral for urgent visit, appointment arranged for 2/14. Return for eye pain, red eye, worsening vision, flashes, floaters or a curtain over vision.

Emergency medicine attending

documents.title: Ophthalmology Consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Ophthalmology consultation, 02/14/2025. Seen at the request of the emergency department; copy to primary care.

Thank you for sending Mr. Morrow, a 27-year-old with Marfan syndrome and bilateral ectopia lentis since childhood, seen two days ago in the ED after his right vision shifted on rubbing the eye. No pain.

Examination: right lens subluxated superonasally, more than the left. The left lens subluxation appears stable from his description of childhood findings. Both lenses remain behind the iris; no lens in the anterior chamber or vitreous. Intraocular pressure normal in both eyes. Anterior chambers quiet. Dilated fundus exam: retina attached in both eyes, no tears or holes, optic nerves healthy.

Assessment: bilateral ectopia lentis, recent progression on the right.

Plan: refraction updated and new spectacle prescription provided. Observation. He should avoid rubbing his eyes. Lens surgery would be considered only if his vision cannot be adequately corrected with glasses. Return immediately for flashes, new floaters or a curtain in his vision. Recheck in 6 months.

Meds reviewed: metoprolol succinate, lisinopril, aspirin. Allergies: NKDA.

Ophthalmology

events.reason: Follow-up after ED visit for vision change

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED f/u. 2/12 R eye vision change after rubbing it -- ED found the right lens shifted further superonasally, no abrasion. Ophtho saw him 2/14: both lenses behind the iris, pressures normal, retina attached, new glasses ordered, observation.

Today: right eye still a bit blurry until the new glasses come in, otherwise fine. No pain, no flashes or floaters. Cardiac: no new symptoms, same mild stair intolerance.

Pulse pressure still wide. Diastolic murmur at LSB. Lungs clear.

A/P: Ectopia lentis with R progression -- glad he finally has an ophthalmologist; keep the 6 month recheck. Reviewed the retinal detachment warning signs again. Cardiac issues unchanged, cardiology echo due in August. Meds same.

documents.title: Refills before I travel
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I'm going to be at my parents' for most of July. Could the pharmacy fill all 3 of my meds early so I don't run out?

documents.title: RE: Refills before I travel
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called the pharmacy and they will do a vacation override on the metoprolol, lisinopril and aspirin. Should be ready by tomorrow afternoon.

reports.text:
Comparison: 08/21/2024.
LV normal in size with normal wall motion; LVEF 60%.
Trileaflet aortic valve; severe aortic regurgitation, unchanged from prior.
Aortic root 4.2 cm at the sinuses, no interval change. Ascending aorta not dilated.
Mitral valve prolapse, mild MR.
Normal RV size and function. No effusion.
reports.conclusion: No interval change: aortic root 4.2 cm, severe AR, MVP with mild MR, LVEF 60%.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP -- ANNUAL FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 08/20/2025

Interval: ED visit in February for right lens subluxation, managed by ophthalmology. No cardiac events. Denies chest pain or syncope.

Echo today: aortic root 4.2 cm, unchanged; severe AR, unchanged; MVP with mild MR; LVEF 60%.

Assessment/plan: Marfan syndrome with stable root aneurysm and severe AR. Continue metoprolol succinate 50 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, aspirin 81 mg daily. Activity restrictions as before. Echo and visit in 12 months.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Defending his thesis in the spring. Cardiology in August: no change on echo (root 4.2, severe AR, MVP mild MR, EF 60%), meds the same, next echo in a year. Vision fine with the new glasses.

ROS: tires with long stair climbs as before; no chest or back pain, no fainting, no palpitations lately. Mood fine, PHQ-2 1.
Meds: metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 10, aspirin 81. NKDA. Flu/covid done 10/9.

Exam: tall, thin, NAD. Eyes: glasses, no redness. Heart: diastolic murmur at LSB, regular rhythm. Lungs clear. Abd benign. Ext no swelling. Skin clear.

A/P: chronic issues stable and followed by cardiology and ophthalmology. Labs CMP/CBC. Reinforced: ED for any sudden severe chest, back or belly pain. Return in a year.
